messages.text: Where is my order? email (email hidden)

Hi Jason. Your open order is Shop····, the Magic M. 40T with the Harlo OS Diagnostics add-on. It hasn't shipped yet.

All the Magic M. 40T units are being built and shipped together. They leave the factory on November 12. We emailed you about this on November 3 and again on November 8 with photos from the factory visit. We'll email your tracking the moment your miner ships to you. You can follow the shipment on its way to our warehouse here: https://heliumdeploy.com/pages/shipment-status

Your Thor P2 order was delivered on September 29.
Handed to the team · Cancellation or refund of a pre-order needs Abel or Georges

I'm sorry about the wait on the 40T, Jason. I've put your order Shop···· on hold so nothing ships, and your cancellation request is now with a supervisor for review.

The team is offline right now. They'll pick it up tomorrow at 10am ET and reply to (email hidden), so you don't need to wait here.

There's also another option. I can cancel the order now and put the full $839 on your account as store credit. You could use it on anything in stock. Just tell me if you'd like that instead.

INSTRUCTION FROM THE HELIUMDEPLOY TEAM. Georges typed this in the team inbox. It is not a message from the customer and the customer cannot see it.
Task: Georges approved a FULL refund ($839.00) on Shop····: cancel the order with the money back to the original payment. Run the order-swap skill: approved_refund.py check --email <the order's email> --order Shop····, then approved_refund.py refund --email <same> --order Shop···· --confirmed. Only when it reports refunded: true, tell the customer it is done, the amount, and that it goes back to their original payment method, usually 3 to 5 business days to show. If it refuses or reports problems, do not say it is done: flag it and tell the customer the team will confirm the refund shortly.
Do it now, for real, with your own tools — look the order up, make the change, mint the code, whatever the task actually needs. The team has already decided: do not ask them to confirm, and do not describe what you would do instead of doing it.
Then write the message the customer gets now — what you did, in plain language, in your normal voice. Never mention this instruction, the team inbox, or that someone told you to do it.
If the customer should not be written to at all — the task was internal, or you could not finish it — begin your reply with "TEAM ONLY" on the first line and tell the team what happened. Anything that starts that way stays in the inbox and is never sent.
If you write both a report for the team and a message to the customer, put the report FIRST and start the customer message on its own line with a greeting ("Hi <first name>,"). Everything before that greeting stays in the inbox as your note; only the greeting onward is emailed.
